question.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.9 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0.6 & 0.6\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above, what is the value of $a+b-c?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.9 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0.6 & 0.6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 \\ 0.1 & -0.8 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0.6 & -0.4\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.1 & 0.2 & 0.3 & 0 \\ 0.1 & -0.8 & 0.1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.6 & -0.4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=10{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=10{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+2(\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{13}{3}{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{3}{x}_{3}+\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ 6{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{18} \\ \frac{1}{9} \\ \frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b-c=\frac{13}{18}+\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$
